---
title: "Use a trained model in a dashboard or fitting script"
---

A portable artifact includes weights, architecture, ordered column names, time
grid, training-only scaling, training bounds, configuration, history, package
versions and dataset fingerprints. Loading does not need the original simulation
bank or Hydra YAML.

```python
from metis import Surrogate
model = Surrogate.load("surrogate.pt", device="cpu")
result = model.predict({"contact_rate": 0.4, "recovery_rate": 0.1})
```

Load once when a dashboard starts, then call `predict` for user-selected inputs.
For stochastic models use `sample` to display individual realizations or call
`predict(..., n_samples=100)` for an explicitly requested Monte Carlo mean.
Outputs are NumPy arrays in original units. Labels and times are available on
the model object; the package does not force a web framework or plotting system.

A training grid is part of the artifact: changing its horizon or timepoints
requires a compatible new model. Input-range warnings indicate extrapolation;
they do not certify predictions inside the ranges. The high-level interface
currently accepts static inputs. Sequence conditioning is an advanced module
feature rather than an inferred meaning of a changing input column.

## Approximate likelihoods

For `itarflow`, `log_prob(inputs, outputs)` returns the full learned density in
original output units, including normalization's Jacobian and the Gaussian
constant. `log_prob_tensor` preserves gradients for use in an external fitting
or inference routine. Argument order is inputs, outputs; inputs have shape
`(batch, parameters)` and outputs `(batch, timepoints, outputs)`.

The returned value is a continuous surrogate density. Integer counts,
conservation relationships, observation noise and simulator discrepancy require
explicit modelling decisions before treating it as a scientific likelihood.
The package does not quietly add an observation model or infer a posterior.
Check identifiability, predictive calibration and sensitivity to surrogate error
for the intended inference problem.

## Compatibility and inspection

Use `input_names`, `output_names`, `times`, `training_metadata`, `history`,
`model_config`, `parameter_count` and the fitted scalers to inspect a model.
The underlying PyTorch module is available as `model.model` for advanced use.
Artifacts have an explicit format version and allowlisted model families;
loading uses PyTorch's restricted weights-only loader. Keep artifact versions
and package versions with published scientific results.
